> Runtime: median of --runs measured runs (default 7); the 95% confidence interval, standard deviation and any outlier samples are in latest.json.
> Peak memory: highest sampled working set while the program ran, per language; interpreted languages therefore include their VM.
> Executable: the built binary file in bytes (lsaca, C, Rust only). Python and Node.js are interpreted and have no ahead-of-time build.
> Cold build: median of --compile-repeats cold builds (default 3) from a fresh cache directory for lsaca; one --compile-repeats median for gcc and rustc. In fallback build mode the lsaca cold column is the emit-c + gcc total.

## Independent oracle verification

scripts/oracles.py holds independent Python reference implementations of every workload. Before measuring, the harness recomputed 12 program checksums and 15 data-scale checksums from those references; mismatches: 0.

A mismatch aborts the run before any measurement is taken, so a published result always has all language outputs agreeing with the independent reference.

Targets are the v2.0 performance acceptance criteria: every measured aspect within 1.4x of C (or documented), a hello-sized cold build of 0.35-0.5 s, a cached build of about 15 ms, and compile_large at no more than 2.5x the reference C build. The cold-build proxy is the smallest single-file workload in the suite; once a dedicated hello workload is added, use it instead.

### Documented exceptions and limitations

v2.0 final is above the 1.4x-of-C target on 9 of 12 compared workloads.

| workload | x C | documented reason |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| string_build | 4.91 | to be documented in Fairness notes |
| binary_trees | 18.76 | by-value workload: each recursive step builds and returns a subtree by value, so deep copies are part of the measured workload by design; `binary_trees_refs` is the comparable reference-traversal variant. |
| binary_trees_refs | 1.78 | to be documented in Fairness notes |
| string_split | 2.47 | to be documented in Fairness notes |
| iterator_pipeline | 2.48 | to be documented in Fairness notes |
| hashmap_wordcount | 1.94 | to be documented in Fairness notes |
| fn_pipeline | 1.42 | to be documented in Fairness notes |
| string_unicode | 20.00 | to be documented in Fairness notes |
| hashmap_string | 1.49 | to be documented in Fairness notes |

Known semantic limitations (documented, not chased):

- `binary_trees`: by-value workload: each recursive step builds and returns a subtree by value, so deep copies are part of the measured workload by design; `binary_trees_refs` is the comparable reference-traversal variant.
